newsitem.title: USA: Eagle Pacific sees resin costs stabilizing.
newsitem.headline: Eagle Pacific sees resin costs stabilizing.

text.p: Eagle Pacific Industries Inc said Monday it expects resin prices to stabilize somewhat in the second and third quarters, after rising in the first quarter.
Earlier, Eagle Pacific reported first quarter net income of $0.07 per fully diluted share, down from $0.14 a year ago.
Cost of goods sold rose 13 percent to $13.4 million in the first quarter from $11.8 million a year ago, due primarily to higher resin prices and slightly lower selling prices.

"While resin prices have risen in the first quarter, we anticipate them to stabilize somewhat in the second and third quarters of this year," William Spell, chief executive officer, said in a statement.
Eagle Pacific owns Eagle Plastics Inc, Arrow Plastics Inc, and Pacific Plastics Inc, extruders of polyvinyl chloride and polyethylene pipe and tubing products.

Eagle Pacific also said recently it raised $10 million through a private placement of redeemable eight percent convertible preferered stock to Massachusetts Mutual Life Insurance Co. The stock is convertible to common stock at $4.26 a share and will pay an eight percent dividend.
